header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Mike Rogers (CTO, AuroraAI), Elena Park (ML Engineer), Tom Li (Infra Lead), Sana Haddad (Product)
summary: Discovery call to understand AuroraAI's migration needs from current OpenAI-based stack and on-prem experiments with vLLM/TGI. Main concerns: eval parity, latency/cost tradeoffs, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and feasibility of a pilot on Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
topics: Model eval parity and metric alignment
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood, AE on this account. Priya, you want to intro?
[00:08] Priya: Hey all, Priya Nambiar, solutions engineer. We'll try to cover infra constraints and perf expectations.
[00:15] Mike: Hi, Mike Rogers, CTO at AuroraAI. Thanks. Quick background — we've been primarily on OpenAI for prod, but doing on-prem experiments with vLLM and TGI to control cost. Today we want to see if Redwood can be a migration path while keeping eval parity.
[00:30] Jordan: Perfect. High-level — Redwood offers Hosted, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). We'll ask about traffic, SLOs, and any red-team compliance needs.
[00:42] Tom: For infra: 200 rps peak, p95 latency target ~350ms for most prompts, some long-range generation up to 2k tokens. We use quantized Llama variants in prod.
[00:55] Elena: On the eval side, we care about accuracy delta vs OpenAI GPT and Anthropic on our benchmarks, and also prompt fidelity — we saw some hallucination shift when moving to vLLM.
[01:10] Priya: Got it. A couple clarifying q's: when you say "eval parity" do you have a numerical threshold?
[01:18] Elena: Ideally <2% drop in our composite score (BLEU-ish + human fuzz). Also latency increase <20% for critical flows.
[01:28] Jordan: Makes sense. Are you leaning Hosted first or Dedicated/Private?
[01:33] Mike: We want a path: start hosted to iterate quickly, then Dedicated for sustained production, and Private for regulated customers requiring data residency. But need to know how compatible our vLLM/TGI workloads are.
[01:45] Priya: On vLLM/TGI compatibility — Redwood's runtime supports common transformer architectures and we have infra to run both regular FP16 and int8 quantized models. Some kernel-level differences mean you might see small perf delta vs native vLLM in early steps. We can surface kernel choices and recompile paths.
[02:05] Tom: Are you supporting flash attention and other attention kernels that vLLM uses?
[02:10] Priya: Yes, we select kernels based on model arch and sequence length distribution. We also do KV cache management tuned for streaming. Sometimes names get fuzzy in the transcript — it's "key-value cache" not "KV cash" — ha.
[02:25] Mike: Haha. On security, we need SOC2, SSO via SAML, and KMS/HSM for key control. Also VPC peering or on-prem option for the pilot.
[02:36] Jordan: Redwood has SOC2, SSO/SAML support, and KMS integrations. Private deployment supports a customer-controlled control plane in VPC and we can run the on-prem package for air-gapped environments. We'll share the security pack.
[02:50] Elena: Nice. For model parity testing, we currently run model comparison against OpenAI GPT-4o and Anthropic Claude; for community models we use Llama-2 70B and custom fine-tuned versions on vLLM. Will Redwood serve custom finetuned checkpoints?
[03:06] Priya: Yes, we onboard customer checkpoints and support version pinning and rollouts. For fine-tuned models there are quantization/compat nuances — we'll run a compatibility pass. Expect some prompt tuning to match behaviors.
[03:20] Tom: Cost question: Hosted per-token costs vs Dedicated reserved GPUs — at what commit does Dedicated become cheaper?
[03:27] Jordan: There's a curve: for sustained high throughput, Dedicated with reserved GPUs is typically 30–50% cheaper on per-token cost depending on model size and utilization. We'll send a modelled cost comparison tailored to your traffic.
[03:40] Mike: Great. One of our blockers was API parity — we call OpenAI endpoints heavily and have tooling bound to that API. How different is Redwood's API?
[03:50] Priya: Redwood's API is REST/SDK-based and supports chat/generate/embeddings/reranking. We also have a compatibility layer to accept OpenAI-style payloads for easier migration, though some features like tool-calling map slightly differently.
[04:06] Elena: Can we run our OpenAI prompt templates without change?
[04:09] Priya: Usually yes for standard chat prompts; you may need to tweak temperature or system prompt framing during parity tests.
[04:20] Jordan: Also note streaming hooks and token-level cost breakdowns are available in Console for debugging.
[04:28] Mike: Ok. On benchmarks: we want vLLM/TGI parity — like run our Llama-2 70B quantized on Redwood and on our vLLM infra and compare latency and quality.
[04:40] Priya: We can run benchmarks in Hosted using your checkpoint or on a Dedicated test pool; we'll provide a CSV loader for prompt sets and a script to compute your composite score. We'll want a few representative request traces.
[04:55] Tom: Network egress: with Private we want no egress to internet for certain customers. Is that possible?
[05:01] Jordan: Yes, Private/on-prem can be configured air-gapped. VPC options allow private peering too. We'll clarify exact network topology in the technical deep dive.
[05:14] Mike: SLA questions: for Dedicated do you offer SLOs on latency?
[05:19] Priya: We have SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for Dedicated; specifics depend on committed capacity and model profile. For Hosted we offer best-effort with transparent latency percentiles.
[05:31] Elena: On observability, do you provide token-level cost and tracing?
[05:35] Jordan: Yes, Console gives token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. You can tie eval regressions to prompt sets.
[05:44] Mike: Any known issues with TGI models? We use TGI for some generative flows.
[05:50] Priya: TGI integration typically works, but because TGI has its own attention kernels, sometimes perf differs. We'll run a compatibility test specifically for TGI artifacts.
[05:59] Mike: How about model size limits on Hosted?
[06:03] Jordan: Hosted supports many model sizes; extremely large models might need Dedicated or multi-GPU with partitioning. We'll recommend target variants.
[06:12] Tom: We want to preserve our prompt logging for auditability but redact PII before it leaves our infra. Can Redwood accept redacted payloads or run the redaction pre-ingest?
[06:24] Priya: You can do pre-ingest redaction or use Private with in-VPC processing. We also have options to filter logs and configure retention.
[06:33] Sana: From product: timeline — if we start pilot in April, what's realistic?
[06:38] Jordan: Quick hosted pilot can start within 1–2 weeks after contracts; Dedicated or Private pilot (VPC setup + infra) typically 4–8 weeks depending on network provisioning and legal review.
[06:51] Elena: For the eval metrics, we'll share our script. Do you accept human eval scores in addition to automated metrics?
[06:58] Priya: Absolutely — we can ingest human scores and the Console supports custom metric dashboards for regression alerts.
[07:08] Mike: Ok, objections: our compliance team will push back on hosted for PII-heavy workloads; that's why Private matters. Also cost of migrating thousands of prompt templates is nontrivial.
[07:22] Jordan: Understood. Pilot approach: run a subset of flows in Hosted for speed, validate parity then move to Dedicated/Private for regulated traffic. We'll prepare a migration checklist.
[07:35] Tom: For the technical deep dive, can Priya's team run a 2-hour session to map network, firewall rules, and IAM?
[07:42] Priya: Yes; we'll schedule with your infra. We'll bring a runbook and example Terraform snippets for VPC peering.
[07:50] Mike: Any references from customers who've migrated from OpenAI and run vLLM on-prem?
[07:56] Jordan: We have a couple of case studies — one fintech that moved to Dedicated and another healthcare customer using Private. I'll share redacted case studies and ROI numbers.
[08:07] Elena: About quantization — we saw semantic drift with int8 in vLLM for some fine-tuned weights. How do you recommend handling that?
[08:17] Priya: We recommend evaluation with multiple quantization profiles; Redwood Optimize suggests quant/FP mixes per workload. For critical flows, keep a higher-precision variant behind a canary.
[08:30] Mike: Good. Legal/procurement: what paperwork do we need for a Dedicated trial?
[08:36] Jordan: Standard MSA/SSA and NDA; procurement usually needs the SOW for Dedicated capacity. We'll loop legal and share templates.
[08:45] Sana: We'll need the security pack for our vendor review.
[08:48] Jordan: Will send SOC2 report, encryption docs, and KMS integration notes.
[08:55] Mike: Last quick thing — do you support model rollbacks if a new model introduces regressions?
[08:59] Priya: Yes, version pinning and rollback are first-class; you can do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to compatible variants.
[09:08] Jordan: Ok let's recap.
[09:10] Priya: Recap: Jordan will send pricing + case studies and security pack; Priya will prepare benchmark plan and scripts; AuroraAI to share prompts and eval targets; schedule technical deep dive for VPC details.
[09:27] Mike: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:30] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and links.
[09:35] Speaker 1: (background noise) thanks.
[47:50] Jordan: (end) Closing notes — action items captured.

Notes: transcript contains a few transcription artifacts; product names sometimes transcribed oddly (e.g., "v L L M", "tee gee eye"). Links referenced: pricing sheet (link to be sent), security pack (link to be sent), benchmark CSV template (to be shared).
